name: Agent Memory and Planning
blurb: How agents remember, plan, and recover.

repos.name: mem0
repos.description: Universal memory layer for AI Agents

repos.name: letta
repos.description: Platform for stateful agents: AI with advanced memory that can learn and self-improve over time.

reading.body:
Mem0 alone accounts for more than two-thirds of the combined 93,824 stars across these three repositories, making it the clear centre of gravity in open-source agent memory as of August 2026.

All three projects carry Apache-2.0 licences, which removes a common friction point for teams integrating memory layers into production systems. All three were pushed within the same nine-day window in late August 2026, suggesting active and concurrent development rather than a stagnant field. The gap between mem0 at 64,433 stars and letta at 24,508 is substantial, though star counts reflect developer attention more than deployment scale or technical completeness.

For AI specifically, persistent memory and planning are what separate a stateless language model call from an agent that can act across sessions, recover from interruptions, and accumulate knowledge. That capability shift has direct implications for compute: an agent that retrieves and updates memory on every turn adds inference calls, storage reads, and potentially fine-tuning loops that a one-shot query does not. The data does not cover how these projects handle that overhead, what infrastructure they require to run at scale, or how widely they are used outside repositories that star them.
